goal: National Geographic Kids science-reader photos: authentic, species-correct, not cartoon.
avoid: cartoon, kawaii, Pixar, Disney, 3D cute, plastic CGI, oversized eyes, anthropomorphic grin
text, letters, numbers, captions, watermarks, logos, arrows, labels
wrong animals for the word: zebra for stripe, dalmatian for spot, bird-only for beak, shark-movie for fin
style_photo: Photorealistic National Geographic / BBC Earth wildlife documentary still. Real wild dolphin with wet grey skin texture, subtle rake marks, water droplets, scientifically correct anatomy: rounded melon, rostrum, small dark eye, single crescent blowhole on top of the head, pectoral flippers, falcate dorsal fin, horizontal tail flukes (not a fish tail). Natural ocean or river lighting, god rays underwater. No cartoon, no 3D animation, no Pixar, no kawaii, no oversized human-like eyes, no anthropomorphic cartoon smile, no plastic toy look. No text, no letters, no numbers, no watermark, no logo. Child-appropriate educational science photo, no blood.

species_notes.bottlenose: Common bottlenose dolphin Tursiops truncatus: medium-grey, robust body, short-to-moderate beak, prominent falcate dorsal fin.
species_notes.spinner: Spinner dolphin Stenella longirostris: slender, very long narrow beak, three-tone grey, tropical ocean.
species_notes.striped: Striped dolphin Stenella coeruleoalba: dark grey cape, white blaze from eye toward dorsal fin, a distinct dark lateral stripe running from the eye back along the flank toward the anus. NOT a zebra. NOT vertical bars.
species_notes.spotted: Atlantic spotted dolphin Stenella frontalis: dark spots on the pale belly and pale spots on the darker back in adults.
species_notes.boto: Amazon river dolphin Inia geoffrensis (boto): pink to pink-grey, very long toothy beak, flexible neck, low dorsal ridge instead of a tall triangular fin, paddle-like flippers, in tannin-brown river with flooded forest.

story.en: There are many kinds of dolphins.
story.scene: Educational but photorealistic underwater-and-surface documentary composition showing several REAL dolphin species that look clearly different from one another in one wide ocean scene: a bottlenose dolphin, a long-beaked spinner dolphin, a striped dolphin with its true dark flank stripe, an Atlantic spotted dolphin with real spots, and in a slightly more coastal/river-mouth area a pink Amazon river dolphin. Natural lighting, not a collage with hard cutouts. Looks like a National Geographic science spread photograph. Many kinds of dolphins, biodiversity.

Close underwater side-view of spinner dolphins (Stenella longirostris) with very long, slender, protruding beaks/rostrums clearly the visual focus. Tropical blue water, natural skin texture. The long beak must be unmistakable compared with a bottlenose.

Close underwater side-view of common bottlenose dolphins showing their shorter, thicker, stubbier beaks/rostrums as the visual focus. Grey wet skin, natural. Clearly a shorter beak than a spinner dolphin. Open ocean, photoreal.

A small pod of REAL striped dolphins (Stenella coeruleoalba) swimming together. Show the authentic field-mark: a dark stripe from the eye along the side of the body, plus the pale blaze. NOT cartoon vertical stripes. NOT zebras. NOT common-dolphin hourglass unless accurate. Sunlit blue water, documentary photo.

One Atlantic spotted dolphin (Stenella frontalis) in clear water, adult with obvious dark spots on the pale underside and light spots on the darker back. Close enough to read the spots. Photoreal wildlife photo, not a dalmatian, not painted polka dots.

Bottlenose or spinner dolphins in the open ocean: deep blue pelagic water, waves, bright sky at the surface, no jungle river. A wild ocean habitat, documentary over-under or at the surface with the pod.

Amazon river dolphins (Inia geoffrensis, botos) in a wide brown tannin-stained tropical river, flooded forest and tree roots, pink-grey bodies, long beaks, low dorsal ridge not a tall ocean dorsal fin. Split-level river surface and underwater. Real freshwater habitat, not the open ocean.

story.en: All dolphins have flippers, a fin, and a tail.
story.scene: A clear full-body side photograph of a wild bottlenose dolphin underwater so THREE body parts are all obviously visible at once: two pectoral flippers, the triangular falcate dorsal fin on the back, and the horizontal tail flukes. Educational anatomy photo, no labels, no text.
A tight pod of bottlenose dolphins swimming in coordinated formation through clear blue water, bodies parallel, social group travel. Documentary wildlife photo.

story.en: They work as a team to hunt fish.
story.scene: Bottlenose dolphins cooperatively herding a dense bait-ball school of small silver fish (sardines). Team hunting behavior, circling and packing the fish, no blood, no torn prey. National Geographic feeding-strategy photo.

story.en: Dolphins like to play with things they find in the water.
story.scene: A wild bottlenose dolphin playing with a long ribbon of brown-green kelp/seaweed, tossing or carrying it. Documented natural play behavior. Clear water, photoreal, not a plastic toy ball.

story.en: They also like to leap and jump.
story.scene: A wild bottlenose dolphin fully breaching, leaping high above the ocean surface, body arched, spray and droplets, blue sea and sky. Powerful real leap, wildlife photography, not a cartoon jump.
A bottlenose dolphin at the ocean surface with its blowhole clearly open on top of the head, exhaling a misty spout of air and water. Shows they are air-breathing mammals. Photoreal, sky and water.

story.en: They come to the top of the water to get air.
story.scene: Dolphins surfacing, heads and blowholes breaking the top of the water to inhale, ripples and splashes, bright sky. Coming up for air, documentary.
A bottlenose dolphin diving steeply head-first from the glittering surface down into deep blue water, trail of bubbles from the tail, powerful dive. The whole body angled downward. Wildlife photo.

words.ex: There are many kinds of dolphins.
words.scene: A single wild common bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops truncatus) swimming underwater, full body side view, scientifically accurate grey coloring darker on the back and paler below, wet skin, natural ocean blue background slightly out of focus. Iconic, clear dolphin portrait.
Wide open ocean: deep blue sea, waves, horizon, sunlight. A wild dolphin dorsal fin or a small pod in the open pelagic ocean. Emphasize OCEAN habitat, not a river.
A tropical freshwater RIVER with brown-green water, jungle banks, and a pink Amazon river dolphin (boto) surfacing. Clearly a river, not the sea.
Wild bottlenose dolphin diving steeply downward, head pointed to the depths, bubbles streaming up. Action of diving.
Bottlenose dolphin swimming horizontally with a strong tail-fluke stroke, streamlined, bubbles, clear water. The action of swimming.

words.ex: They work as a team to hunt fish.
words.scene: Dolphins hunting: chasing and herding a school of silver fish underwater. Cooperative hunt, no blood. Focus on hunting behavior.
Wild dolphin playing with floating kelp, pushing or tossing seaweed. Natural play, not a beach ball, not children.

words.ex: They like to leap and jump.
words.scene: Bottlenose dolphin leaping high out of the ocean, full body in the air, splash below. The leap is the subject.

Close-up wildlife photo of a dolphin's PECTORAL FLIPPER (the side paddle-like limb), anatomically correct, grey wet skin, water. Not a scuba diving fin worn by a human unless very secondary. The animal flipper is the hero.
A dolphin DORSAL FIN cutting the ocean surface, falcate curved triangle, grey, with the back of a bottlenose just under the water. Real dolphin fin, not a horror-movie shark fin, not a fish.
Close-up of dolphin TAIL FLUKES: horizontal, two-lobed, notched in the middle, lifting from the water or powering a stroke. Mammal flukes, NOT a vertical fish tail.

words.ex: There are many kinds of dolphins.
words.scene: From a small research boat, a person points toward wild dolphins in the distance on the ocean. Sense of 'there they are'. Photoreal, not a cartoon child.

words.ex: There are many kinds of dolphins.
words.scene: A LARGE pod: many dolphins, a dozen or more, filling the frame underwater or at the surface. Emphasize quantity, many animals.
Tight close-up of a dolphin's BEAK/rostrum: jaws, teeth slightly visible, melon above, real skin texture. Dolphin beak, NOT a bird, NOT a duck.
Side portrait of a spinner dolphin with a noticeably LONG slender beak dominating the composition. The length of the beak is the point.
Side portrait of a bottlenose dolphin with a SHORT thick beak, clearly stubbier than a spinner. The shortness of the beak is the point.
Full-body bottlenose dolphin underwater clearly possessing flippers, a dorsal fin, and a tail, as if showing what dolphins have. Clean educational wildlife photo.
THESE striped dolphins in the foreground, a small group of Stenella coeruleoalba with real flank stripes, close to the camera. Demonstrative 'these ones'.

Close wildlife photo of a STRIPED DOLPHIN's flank: the authentic dark lateral stripe from the eye along the body. Real Stenella coeruleoalba field mark. NOT a zebra, NOT a tiger, NOT candy stripes, NOT vertical bars on a cartoon dolphin.
SOME dolphins (a few) in the open ocean in the foreground, with empty blue water beyond, suggesting a subset. Photoreal pod of three or four.
Dolphins living in their ocean home: swimming in a natural marine habitat with light from the surface. Habitat of living, not a house.
THIS one Atlantic spotted dolphin centered and closest to the camera, other water empty. Singular focus, 'this dolphin'.
Close-up of Atlantic spotted dolphin SKIN with real organic spots, mottled natural pattern. Dolphin spots, NOT a dalmatian dog, NOT a ladybug, NOT painted circles.
The OTHER kind: pink Amazon river dolphins in a river, contrasting with the idea of ocean dolphins. Freshwater boto habitat.
Three or four dolphins swimming tightly together, bodies almost touching, social togetherness.
Dolphins working: cooperatively circling a fish school, coordinated effort, serious hunting work, no blood.
A TEAM of dolphins in a coordinated hunting formation around fish, teamwork visible, several animals acting as one unit.
A dolphin WITH a piece of seaweed, holding or swimming with it. The 'with' relationship: dolphin and object together.

words.ex: Things they find in the water.
words.scene: A dolphin investigating a natural THING in the water: a kelp blade, a drifting coconut, or a jellyfish-safe object. Curiosity toward an object.
THEY: two wild dolphins side by side looking toward the camera/slightly off, a pair as the pronoun they. Photoreal.

words.ex: They find things in the water.
words.scene: A dolphin fully immersed in clear WATER, caustics and light rays, the water itself beautiful and obvious. Underwater world.
Real ocean SEAWEED/kelp forest: long brown-green fronds waving, a dolphin weaving through kelp. Macroalgae, not cartoon grass.
A dolphin clearly enjoying play with kelp at the surface, energetic natural play that reads as 'like / enjoy'. No heart icons, no text.
Close-up of the single crescent BLOWHOLE on top of a dolphin's head, possibly exhaling spray. Accurate mammal blowhole, top of head, not a nose on the snout.

words.ex: A fin on the dolphin's back.
words.scene: View of a dolphin's BACK from above or behind: smooth grey back with the dorsal fin rising from it. The back is the subject.
Dolphin oriented head-DOWN, descending into darker blue, bubbles going up. Direction: down.
Air and mist spraying THROUGH a dolphin's open blowhole at the surface. Motion of air passing through the hole.
Dolphin at the surface taking a breath of AIR, sky visible, spray, chest expanded. Air-breathing at the interface of water and sky.
Dolphin surfacing to BREATHE, blowhole open, inhale/exhale, droplets. The act of breathing.
A dolphin swimming urgently upward toward the bright surface because it needs to breathe, determined ascent from the depths.
Dolphins COMING up from below toward the shining water surface, approaching the top. Movement toward the viewer/surface.

words.ex: Come to the top of the water.
words.scene: Dolphin heads at the TOP of the water, the surface line, sky above, bodies below. The top/surface is clear.
A dolphin GETTING a breath of air, just after inhaling at the surface, water sheeting off the head. Obtaining air.
